title: Urgent Debugging Session: KAS API Failure

sections.text: Okay, the KAS API is down. It's throwing 500 errors on every query. What's going on?
I'm looking. The... the logs show... wait. It's a database connection error. 'Too many clients already'.
Too many clients? How? We have a connection pool. It should... it should handle that.
I know, right? But the, um, the active connections are spiking to max. It's like they're not being... uh... released.
Not released? Did someone push a change? Taylor, did your chunking experiment go live?
No! No, no, that's still on a dev branch. It's... wait. Jamie, did you... did you check the new summarization service?
The what? Oh, the... the background job that generates summaries for old meetings? I... I think that deployed yesterday.
And how does it connect to the DB? Does it use the main API's connection pool or... or does it create its own?
Uh... oh, no. I think... I think it creates its own. Per-per-per-per worker.
Per worker? And how many workers are there?
Twenty. So twenty workers are each spinning up their own connection pool. That's our problem. That's exhausting the database limit.
Okay. Okay, good. We found it. Jamie, kill that service. Now. We'll redeploy it after it's fixed to use a single, shared connection client.
Doing it. Killing the deployment... now.
Phew. Okay. That was... that was close.
